title: Level Shifter Model
constraints: Behavioral model of a low → high voltage level shifter with an input Schmitt trigger. `vin` swings between 0 and `vddl`, and `vout` is either 0.0 or exactly `vddh`.
Output goes high when `vin > 0.6·vddl` and low when `vin < 0.4·vddl`. In between it **holds** its previous value (hysteresis). The initial value is low.
If the low-voltage domain is off (`vddl < 0.3`), `vout = 0.0` and the stored state resets to low (a built-in isolation, as in an enable-type level shifter).
`vout` must follow the inputs combinationally (no clock). Not synthesizable (real numbers).
hints: Keep the state in a variable updated whenever an input changes: `always @(vin or vddl or vddh)` in SystemVerilog, or a process sensitive to all three inputs in VHDL.
Update the state first (off → low, above 0.6 → high, below 0.4 → low), then drive `vout = state ? vddh : 0.0`.
Hysteresis gives noise immunity when the input edge is slow or noisy.
